the_fix.symptom: on both cards the two-line value on row 2 collided with its own key
the_fix.cause: val/.style used anchor=west, which centres the node box on its y, so a two-line value grew upward into the key above it; one-line values did not
the_fix.brief_specified_fix: anchor=north west, every value at its key's y minus 0.30cm
the_fix.fix_actually_used: every node is a single line anchored base west; the two-line value is two nodes instead of one node with a line break; every step inside a row is 0.33cm
why_the_deviation: Built, the briefed 0.30cm removes the collision but lowers each value until it sits closer to the NEXT key than to its own, so every value reads as the heading of the row beneath it. Within-row spacing becomes larger than between-row spacing on both gaps.

More seriously, no offset is a constant of the figure. anchor=north west keeps align=left, and TikZ's align option typesets the node in a minipage whose first-line height follows the ambient \baselineskip. The same coordinates printed about 2.2pt apart between a \normalsize paragraph and a \small line, and about 3.7pt apart between a test harness and Chapter 3. Any offset tuned in one context is wrong in another, so calibrating one would have hidden the fault rather than fixed it.

base west anchoring removes both problems: no centring, no minipage, no dependence on ascenders, descenders or surrounding prose. Key-to-value leading is identical on all three rows and both cards by construction, which is what the brief asked for.

offset_sweep_that_rejected_0.30.method: character-level ink boxes via tools/_measure_frames.py, all variants inside one PDF, card set as a float after \normalsize prose
offset_sweep_that_rejected_0.30.caveat: ink-gap numbers are comparable only WITHIN one PDF; glyph boxes reported by the extractor shift by a constant ~2.1pt between PDFs with different font subsets. Baselines, not ink boxes, are the invariant.
offset_sweep_that_rejected_0.30.note_published_r1: -0.02 is the descender of 'predicted' level with the ascender of 'profile'; they sit at different x and do not touch. r2 = -3.02 is the visible collision.
offset_sweep_that_rejected_0.30.note_r3: r3 reads looser at every offset because 'where chance sits' has no descender and '0.50' is lining figures; node geometry is identical to r1 and r2.
